answer: A concrete Sybil defence in an AI-agent economy is a cost-bearing stake plus a per-identity rate cap. To join, an agent posts a bond that is slashed when its proofs fail, and the protocol limits how much work or reward one identity can claim per window. Because rewards follow bonded value while seats do not, minting N cheap keys buys no extra throughput, only N stakes at risk. Attack cost grows linearly with N, so a farmer needs capital he can lose. One bonded opal key acts as the reef filtering fakes; every copy just burns ember-like money.
